messages:
sanjay: quick heads-up — ran ONNX export + int6 quant on the candidate embedding model and seeing a small but consistent hit on recall@1 for the multilingual holdout. wondering if this is noise or a pattern :thinking:

tessa: hmm, can you paste the eval command you ran? also which dataset slice (short vs long queries)?

sanjay: command I used:
```bash
python eval/recall.py --model models/new-embed-v3.onnx --quant int6 --dataset holdout_multilang_v2 --k 1,10 --buckets length:short,medium,long
```
ran on the nightly cluster (gpu-2). baseline float32 recall@1 = 0.713, int6 recall@1 = 0.691. recall@10 is mostly stable (0.902 -> 0.895).

embed-ci-bot: automated run results attached (sanjay/nightly/1719618230):
- float32: recall@1=0.713, recall@10=0.902, silhouette=0.421
- onnx+int6: recall@1=0.691, recall@10=0.895, silhouette=0.358
(run time: 45m)

noah: silhouette drop is interesting — suggests cluster quality degraded, not just random noise. which languages are the worst?

sanjay: quick breakdown by lang: en -0.9% @1, es -2.6%, fr -1.8%, ko -5.2%, vi -6.1% (low-resource langs hit more).

li: could be quantization scale bias for long tails. do we do per-channel quant or global?

sanjay: used per-tensor symmetric quant from our onnx-quant tool (default). haven't tried per-channel yet.

tessa: try per-channel + range calibration with outlier trimming (p99.9) — same script but add --quant-mode per-channel --calib-trim 0.999

noah: also run the roundtrip cosine check: compute cosine(original_float, dequantized_int6) per-example and bucket by length. if long docs dequantize worse that's a clue.

sanjay: ran quick roundtrip: average cos float->dequant = 0.987 overall, but for long queries avg=0.965 vs short=0.992. distribution has a fat tail at 0.88 for some long examples.

embed-ci-bot: visualizations generated: umap_multilang_float.png vs umap_multilang_int6.png attached. cluster overlap metric: 0.81 -> 0.67.

li: could be that tokenization/position embedding dynamics create larger magnitude components for long inputs that get clipped by int6. can we normalize before quant and evaluate? e.g., L2-normalize pre-quant?

tessa: good call — also try calibrating on a mixed-length sample rather than average-length only.

noah: propose quick plan: 1) run per-channel quant + p99.9 trim 2) add L2-normalize pre-quant 3) run calibration with stratified lengths 4) compute per-lang recall and roundtrip cos. I'll slot a job on small cluster.

sanjay: thanks — if per-channel + normalization recovers most of the drop we can proceed with an ONNX+int6 canary. if not, fallback to int8 or fall back to float for long-doc route.

embed-ci-bot: scheduled jobs:
- 1719618400 run: per-channel+p99.9 (expected 30m)
- 1719618600 run: per-channel+L2norm+stratified-calib (expected 40m)

noah: also leaving a quick note to add a small regression test to nightly: recall@1 delta per-lang must be > -1.5% otherwise fail build (we can tune threshold).

tessa: created ENGML-9883 to track followups (include artifacts + umap images + per-example worst-cases). assigning to @sanjay. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: great — I'll post the job outputs here once done. thanks all :coffee:
